section: Tax planning for the self-employed in Germany (Steueroptimierung)
wording: The statutory rules behind the usual ways a self-employed person in Germany lowers income tax, trade tax, VAT and social contributions: for each idea the rule, its conditions, its limit and what stops it. This Guide never computes a saving and does not rank options. Figures are for tax year 2026, from the federal law pages, the ministry instructions for the 2026 EÜR form (ministry letter of 1 September 2026) and 2026 pension insurer pages. One source is dated another year: the ministry booklet "Steuern von A bis Z" is the 2025 edition, used only for the marginal income tax rates, the church tax rates and the lowest trade tax multiplier, because the statute prints those as factors, not at all, or already in its 2027 version. Rates set for later years are marked as not for 2026.
disposition: Exact original current unit; native coordinates rebound

wording: Read the conditions before the benefit. Several rules only move tax to a later year: the investment deduction is added back when the asset is bought, faster depreciation leaves less for later years, and retained profit is taxed again when withdrawn.

Withdrawals above the year's profit plus deposits trigger the follow-up tax: it defers tax, it does not remove it. Not available for profit on which the § 16(4) EStG allowance or the § 34(3) EStG reduced rate is claimed.

wording: - **§ 1a KStG option.** A commercial or registered civil-law partnership, not a sole trader, may be taxed like a corporation. The initial application is irrevocable and is filed at least one month before the business year. A separate later Rückoption is available under § 1a(4), with its own deemed-conversion consequences. The corporate-tax option ends the EÜR and the § 35 EStG credit. https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__1a.html
disposition: Exact original current unit; native coordinates rebound

wording: - Pay for work really done is an expense (§ 4(4) EStG); household costs and maintenance are not (§ 12 EStG). The arm's-length tests (written contract, payment to the family member's own account, duties matching the pay) come from court rulings, not a linkable page: unverified practice. For a spouse or descendant the collecting agency must ask the pension insurer for a status decision (§ 7a SGB IV). Payroll and the Minijob limit: `de-payroll`. https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__12.html
disposition: Exact original current unit; native coordinates rebound

wording: The base rule is § 4(4) EStG: expenses caused by the business. § 4(5) EStG limits some and points to § 9 EStG. Gifts, entertainment, the home office room and lifestyle-related costs must be recorded singly and apart, or they are lost entirely (§ 4(7) EStG). For mixed costs only the business share counts.

wording:
| Deduction, allowances | For an eligible claimant, own qualifying contributions plus the entitled allowance are capped at EUR 2,100 yearly for the § 10a special-expense comparison. The tax office tests whether that deduction is better than the allowance entitlement; if so, it adds that entitlement back to the tax calculated with the deduction, preventing a double benefit (§ 10a(2)). Basic allowance EUR 175; child allowance EUR 185, or EUR 300 for a child born after 2007, only with the actual § 85 entitlement and allocation below. Allowances are proportionately reduced below the § 86 minimum own contribution. https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__10a.html |

For an isolated directly eligible claimant, with no indirectly eligible spouse, compute the yearly minimum own payment as `max(EUR 60, min(4% × prior-year relevant statutory insured income, EUR 2,100) − entitled basic and child allowances)` (§ 86). Use the actual relevant income category, not turnover or current-year profit. If the actual qualifying own contribution is below that minimum, multiply the entitled allowance by the contribution/minimum ratio; payment at or above the minimum gives the full entitlement. A directly eligible age-30 claimant with no children and prior relevant insured income EUR 20,000 needs EUR 625: min(EUR 800, EUR 2,100) − EUR 175. Paying EUR 312.50 gives EUR 87.50 allowance. With relevant income EUR 100,000, the same claimant needs EUR 1,925. A lower result cannot remove the EUR 60 floor. These are contribution/allowance computations, not a promised tax saving; the actual § 10a tax comparison remains separate.

Document allowance entitlement rather than using child count alone. Under § 85, Kindergeld must be assessed to the entitled person; a full-year total recovery removes that child allowance. If several eligible persons receive Kindergeld for the same child, the first entitlement period in the year determines allocation. For qualifying married, non-separated EU/EEA-resident different-sex parents, allocation is to the mother unless both request the father; for the corresponding same-sex married or civil-partner parents, allocation is to the Kindergeld-assessed parent unless both request the other. That request cannot be withdrawn for an elapsed contribution year. Section 84 adds a one-off EUR 200 to the basic allowance for a directly eligible person under 25 at the start of the contribution year, for the first eligible post-2007 contribution year for which an allowance is requested. The age-30 examples do not include it. Product qualification and indirect-spouse or other eligibility populations require their own actual statutory conditions; voluntary pension contributions alone do not establish the compulsory-insurance branch above.

wording: This Guide presents planning mechanisms and does not rank products or legal forms or calculate a real client's saving. The historical numerical fixtures are retained in the old-topic evidence: their assumed rates and period figures were not reliable current tax results. Official sources need not print a fictional case's numbers for a source-based computation to be valid. For a real comparison apply the actual § 32a tariff with and without the item, including the applicable deductions, caps and interactions; do not assume a constant marginal rate without checking the entire affected taxable-income interval. The five mechanisms below remain. Example 2 stipulates an eligible isolated self-payer with no employer contribution offset or special cap reduction; Example 4 stipulates an actually qualifying independently usable depreciable movable fixed asset. These facts qualify those examples; the general employee pension and asset selectors above still apply.

section: R105 actual employee pension contribution/cap adjustment
wording: For an ordinary employee with qualifying pension contributions, include the actual § 3 no. 62 tax-free employer statutory-pension share or equivalent subsidy in the eligible aggregate under § 10(1) no. 2, apply the actual § 10(3) cap and any statutory special cap reduction, then subtract that tax-free employer part. With employee statutory RV EUR 9,000, qualifying employer RV EUR 9,000 and eligible Basisrente EUR 15,000, the combined EUR 33,000 is capped at EUR 30,826; subtract employer EUR 9,000 to give EUR 21,826, not the employee's whole EUR 24,000. An isolated self-payer has no invented employer offset. Apply the separate cap reduction for the actual pension-free/employer-funded or § 22 no. 4 populations in § 10(3) sentence 3. The specified Minijob employer contributions are added and then subtracted only on the taxpayer's statutory application (§ 10(1) no. 2 sentence 7 and § 10(3) sentence 7).
disposition: New finite sourced ordinary adjustment / labelled separating computation
